items.title: Trailing stops are now available for perp markets.
items.excerpt: A trailing stop's trigger price follows the mark price as it moves in favor of the position. When the mark price retraces from its best level by the selected distance or percentage, it triggers a market order. For long positions, the trigger price follows the highest mark price reached since activation; for short positions, it follows the lowest. An optional activation price determines when tracking begins. Without one, tracking begins immediately at the current mark price.

items.title: In a future network upgrade, HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets.
items.excerpt: This set of additional deployer functionality will collectively be called `HIP-3*`. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. This functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3, and its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release for HIP-3* is currently available on testnet. The specifications on testnet are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback. See https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/hip-3-deployer-actions for more details. As always, Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* is designed to give deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with requirements applicable to them. Like with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators. Deployers use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

items.title: The following updates to the testnet HIP-4 implementation are live, based on builder feedback.
items.excerpt: See https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/hip-4-deployer-actions for details. 1. The `outcomeDeploy` action now has a top-level `venue` field, which is more consistent with the HIP-3 deploy action. This required field is a breaking change on the testnet-only spec. 2. Builder codes can be applied to buy orders for outcome trades, charged in the quote token. These builder fees are charged by the protocol on a best-effort basis. Builder interfaces may validate sufficient quote token balance when computing the maximum order size. There are no changes to spot or perp builder codes. 3. Outcome template metadata going forward include `semanticRestriction` as a field which broadly define the intended semantics of the instantiated market. Markets which contradict their template's semantic restriction are considered malformed and slashable by validators.
items.text:
The following updates to the testnet HIP-4 implementation are live, based on builder feedback. See https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/hip-4-deployer-actions for details.

1. The `outcomeDeploy` action now has a top-level `venue` field, which is more consistent with the HIP-3 deploy action. This required field is a breaking change on the testnet-only spec.
2. Builder codes can be applied to buy orders for outcome trades, charged in the quote token. These builder fees are charged by the protocol on a best-effort basis. Builder interfaces may validate sufficient quote token balance when computing the maximum order size. There are no changes to spot or perp builder codes. 
3. Outcome template metadata going forward include `semanticRestriction` as a field which broadly define the intended semantics of the instantiated market. Markets which contradict their template's semantic restriction are considered malformed and slashable by validators.

The following updates to the testnet HIP-4 implementation are live, based on builder feedback. See https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/hip-4-deployer-actions for details.

1. Sub-deployer permissions allow the deployer to delegate specific permissions to different addresses, similar to HIP-3.
2. The outcome deployment action has been moved from `spotDeploy` to a separate top-level action. This is a breaking change, as occasionally happens with testnet-only specs. 
3. The spot balances precompile supports outcomes. See L1Read.sol at https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interacting-with-hypercore

items.title: Request for feedback on HIP-4 templates: The latest testnet templates can be found onchain, or queried via API via `curl -X POST --header "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{ "type": "outcomeTemplates"}'
items.excerpt: The latest template in each family is available for validator review and vote to be included as a mainnet template. The template families are indexed by an increasing sequence of integer suffixes. For example, `binaryPrice4` is the latest in the `binaryPrice` family. Once feedback is collected, validators will review and vote onchain to initialize the templates for deployer use. The instantiation of all templates will still be gated on HIP-4 itself being enabled on mainnet.
items.text:
Request for feedback on HIP-4 templates: The latest testnet templates can be found onchain, or queried via API via `curl -X POST --header "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{ "type": "outcomeTemplates"}' https://api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/info`. The latest template in each family is available for validator review and vote to be included as a mainnet template. The template families are indexed by an increasing sequence of integer suffixes. For example, `binaryPrice4` is the latest in the `binaryPrice` family.

Once feedback is collected, validators will review and vote onchain to initialize the templates for deployer use. The instantiation of all templates will still be gated on HIP-4 itself being enabled on mainnet.
